overview: Black mirrors with ...c5, an English-style response, and White plays Bb2, e3 and Nf3 with flexible pawn play (c4, d4 or f4) and long-diagonal pressure. The position is a Sicilian-like structure with colours reversed, and Black usually follows with ...Nc6, ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...d5 or ...g6. The play is quiet and manoeuvring, usually equal, with tactics if the diagonals open.

white_ideas.idea: Bb2, e3, Nf3 and Bb5 to pressure e5 and the long diagonal
Choose between c4, d4 and f4 after seeing Black's set-up
Trade the dark-squared bishop or play for a small endgame edge

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Nc6, ...e6, ...Nf6 and hit the centre with ...d5
Fianchetto with ...g6 and ...Bg7 to meet the long diagonal
Equalise with a solid centre and counter on the queenside

typical_structures.structure: Reversed Sicilian / English with ...c5 against b3 and e3, flexible pawn structure

character.notes: Quiet and flexible, low theory; sharpens only if the long diagonal opens.

soundness.notes: Sound; used by super-GMs as a surprise weapon.

structure.notes: Flank opening with centre not fixed; flexible.

approach.notes: A b3/Bb2 set-up White can use against almost anything.

level.notes: Plans are clear but the flexible pawn play needs judgement.

sublines_that_differ.how: Black takes a classical centre and the game becomes a Reversed Sicilian with White's bishop on b2.

character.reason: Quiet manoeuvring with some tactics, neither forcing nor especially hard to break.
